pr_title: refactor(compiler-cli): only use type constructors for directives with generic types
pr_body:
Prior to this change, the template type checker would always use a
type-constructor to instantiate a directive. This type-constructor call
serves two purposes:

1. Infer any generic types for the directive instance from the inputs
   that are passed in.
2. Type check the inputs that are passed into the directive's inputs.

The first purpose is only relevant when the directive actually has any
generic types and using a type-constructor for these cases inhibits
a type-check performance penalty, as a type-constructor's signature is
quite complex and needs to be generated for each directive.

This commit refactors the generated type-check blocks to only generate
a type-constructor call for directives that have generic types. Type
checking of inputs is achieved by generating individual statements for
all inputs, using assignments into the directive's fields.

Even if a type-constructor is used for type-inference of generic types
will the input checking also be achieved using the individual assignment
statements. This is done to support the rework of the language service,
which will start to extract symbol information from the type-check
blocks.

As a future optimization, it may be possible to reduce the number of
inputs passed into a type-constructor to only those inputs that
contribute the the type-inference of the generics. As this is not a
necessity at the moment this is left as follow-up work.

Closes #38185

---

On top of #38226 as it requires that fix for the tests to pass.

issue_context.title: Ivy LS: refactor type constructors and input binding checking
issue_context.body:
Currently input bindings in templates are type-checked via a type constructor call for the directive or component in question. This is mainly for convenience, since type constructors were always called with the inputs present anyway.

This is undesirable for two reasons:
1) Type constructors are expensive, and often unnecessary. They only need to be called if the directive or component is actually generic, and only need those inputs passed which reference the generic type parameters.

2) For language service use cases, it is valuable to have a direct assignment operation for inputs in the TCB in order to extract LS information (e.g. `ts.TypeChecker.getSymbolAtLocation`).

Thus, we should refactor the way input checking works:
* only call type constructors when necessary, and only with those inputs that affect generic type inference
* always emit assignment operations for inputs
* for diagnostics, rely on the type ctor call for generic inputs, and on the assignment operations for non-generic inputs (adding the ignore flag to the others)
comments: @JoostK has a prototype started for this, which he's extracting into a PR.
